Crucial preparation ahead of Test series

India Test captain Shubman Gill was rested on the opening day of India's warm-up match against Sri Lanka XI in Colombo after sustaining an impact injury to his right ring finger during training on Thursday.The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed that the decision was purely precautionary, with the medical team closely monitoring Gill's recovery ahead of the two-Test series."Captain Shubman Gill sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during India's practice on Thursday. KL Rahul will lead the team in Gill's absence ," the board wrote on X.Sri Lanka XI won the toss and opted to bat first in Colombo, giving India's bowlers an opportunity to acclimatise to local conditions before the Test series.Nishan Madushka, Pasindu Sooriyabandara, Pavan Rathnayake, Ahan Wickramasinghe, Sonal Dinusha (c), Anjala Bandara (wk), Nipun Dhananjaya, Lahiru Kumara, Vishwa Fernando, Asanka Manoj, Isitha Wijesundera, Ramesh Mendis, Dilum Sudeera, Keshara Nuwantha, Ravindu Rasantha.Shubman Gill, Yashasvi Jaiswal, Sai Sudharsan, Devdutt Padikkal, KL Rahul (c), Rishabh Pant (wk), Ravindra Jadeja, Dhruv Jurel, Manav Suthar, Saransh Jain, Kuldeep Yadav, Mohammed Siraj, Prasidh Krishna, Auqib Nabi, Gurnoor Brar.The warm-up fixture is India's only red-ball outing before the opening Test, making every session valuable. Head coach Gautam Gambhir urged the squad to maximise the preparation despite the uncertainty surrounding the weather."We know what is in front of us. We can do volume, we can push our limits, we can tick all the boxes and come the 15th morning, whether we are batting first or bowling first, we will be absolutely ready with every answer to every question thrown at us," Gambhir told the players."So make sure to tick all the boxes from now on."
Article Summary: Shubman Gill rested on opening day of India's warm-up match against Sri Lanka XI in Colombo. Captain sustained an impact injury to his right ring finger during training on Thursday. The Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) confirmed that the decision was purely precautionary.

Article Title: India vs Sri Lanka: India's search for answers to rediscover lost glory in Tests begins in Colombo
Article Text:
Gautam Gambhir and Shubman Gill (Image credit: SLC)

TimesofIndia.com in Colombo:

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

"Come 15th morning whether we are batting first or bowling first we will be absolutely ready with every answer to every question thrown at us."India head coach Gautam Gambhir came prepared with the war cry when his troops assembled at the Nondescripts Cricket Club in Colombo for their first practice session on the crucial two-Test tour. The weather stayed clear, allowing the visitors a proper morning hit before another intense session on a very humid afternoon the following day. The Shubman Gill-led unit arrived in Sri Lanka 11 days before the series opener in Galle on August 15.There will be enough practice sessions, including a three-day warm-up fixture, before the first Test, ensuring ample opportunity to acclimatise to the local conditions. Additionally, conditions will be familiar for six of the 15 squad members who were part of two fixtures in the India A vs Sri Lanka A series last month.India have had mixed outings in the longest format over the past year; they drew a series in England (2-2) they would have fancied themselves to win and then suffered a tame surrender against South Africa (0-2).The scheduling meant India lacked ideal preparation for the South Africa series, as they had to adjust to different time zones and formats within a matter of days.The result: a whitewash that left plenty to ponder.Not much changed for the one-off Test against Afghanistan; most players switched from the IPL to the red-ball grind within days, but the opposition did not pose the kind of challenge that could have raised further questions over the scheduling.The questions around scheduling and preparation can well take a back seat this August, as the Test squad is well-rested and has enough time, in the coach's words, to "tick all the boxes" before taking the field in Galle.Though there are some injury concerns. The team are without Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar (at least for the first Test). However, the 14 available players (Sai Sudharsan is yet to receive clearance from the CoE) are fit and raring to go. They also have a variety of net bowlers — Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Vipraj Nigam and Shivang Kumar — to aid their preparations.Ravindra Jadeja has had the longest lean period, having last played in the IPL. Mohammed Siraj and Rishabh Pant have also been cooling their heels since the one-off Test against Afghanistan in June.In the build-up to the series, several players prepared individually: Yashasvi Jaiswal and KL Rahul trained indoors in rain-hit Mumbai, while Shubman Gill had some productive sessions in Chandigarh. Pant flew to Ranchi to spend some time with former India captain MS Dhoni.To keep their World Test Championship final qualification hopes alive, India need to board the flight back from Colombo with a 2-0 series victory.The road in this format has not been smooth; it has been littered with pertinent questions. The next three weeks offer the team management and the squad the opportunity not only to find those answers, but also to rediscover their lost glory.
Article Summary: India have had mixed outings in the longest format over the past year. The scheduling meant India lacked ideal preparation for the South Africa series. The team are without Jasprit Bumrah and Washington Sundar (at least for the first Test). However, the 14 available players are fit and raring to go.

Article Title: Brendon McCullum backs Joe Root, vows to 'develop' Harry Brook into England's next Test captain
Article Text:
(IANS) England white-ball captain Harry Brook and Brendon McCullum

McCullum backs Brook as future Test captain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

McCullum praises new Test coach Stephen Fleming

What's next for England?

England white-ball head coach Brendon McCullum has backed the ECB's decision to reappoint Joe Root as Test captain following Ben Stokes' retirement, while insisting that Harry Brook remains the long-term leadership prospect.Brook, who served as Stokes' deputy during England's recent Test series against New Zealand, was widely viewed as a leading candidate for the captaincy. However, when Stokes missed the second Test after being suspended for breaching the team's curfew, the ECB entrusted the captaincy to former skipper Joe Root instead of Brook. Following Stokes' retirement, the board opted to hand Root a second stint as Test captain.Despite Brook missing out on the role, McCullum believes the 27-year-old's time will come."Everyone knows the affection that I have for Harry, he's a wonderful player and he's doing a fine job as white-ball leader. I think his time will come in the Test job," McCullum told Sky Sports."I'm looking forward to working with him and hopefully growing and developing him into the leader that he can become. At some stage in the future, he will have a very important role in that capacity.But for now, Joe will do an amazing job," he added.While McCullum continues as England's head coach in white-ball cricket, the ECB has appointed former New Zealand captain Stephen Fleming as the new Test coach, ending McCullum's four-year tenure in the red-ball format.Praising his fellow New Zealander, McCullum said Fleming was the ideal choice to take English Test cricket forward."I had a great time in my four years but now it's going in a different direction. I think Flem will be excellent, he's a little bit like me, but better – that's how I would sum him up. He'll do a great job, and the ECB have done incredibly well to get someone like him to commit to English cricket. It's an outstanding achievement, " McCullum said.England's upcoming home Test series against Pakistan will see Marcus Trescothick serve as interim head coach before Fleming officially assumes charge for the tour of South Africa in December 2026.
Article Summary: Brendon McCullum backs Joe Root to succeed Ben Stokes as England Test captain. England white-ball head coach believes Harry Brook's time will come in Test role. McCullum praises new Test coach Stephen Fleming. Fleming will take charge for England's tour of South Africa in 2026.

Article Title: How Harsh fought through pain to script CWG history, now targets Asiad medal
Article Text:
How judoka Harsh overcame pain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Harsh Singh's right knee still swells. It still hurts. Every time the Indian judoka steps onto the mat, he is reminded of the ACL and meniscus tear that nearly derailed his career. But at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow, pain took a back seat as the 23-year-old scripted history by becoming India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist."The pain never really goes away," Singh told TOI in an interview on Thursday. "Sometimes my knee still swells up and feels tight. During the CWG, I felt the pain and the knee occasionally got swollen. After surgery, the joint never became exactly the way it was before. There's always a little discomfort during fights. You have to ignore it and continue. The medal kept me going."The historic triumph came less than a year after Singh tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport (IIS) in Aug 2025. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition."I was in rehabilitation for almost a year. The entire coaching team at the IIS, recovery specialists and Spencer sir (Mackay, S&C expert) helped me throughout.They rebuilt my strength step by step. Because of the IIS and their entire team, I was able to come back on the mat, qualify for the CWG and represent India," he said.The comeback demanded another battle off the mat. Months away from competition saw his weight rise to nearly 72kg, forcing him to shed more than 12kg to return to his 60kg category. Gold at a ranking tournament and bronze at the senior National championships sealed his place in India's CWG squad.Despite lingering discomfort, Singh dominated in Glasgow, with only a hard-fought semifinal stretching him before he clinched the historic title."The semifinal (against the Australian Pedro Carlos) was the toughest. In the 60kg category, even a small point can decide the match. We didn't want to concede anything and stayed aggressive," he recalled.With CWG gold secured, Singh has already shifted his attention to next year's Asian Games. Training stints in Japan and South Korea are part of his preparations as he looks to bridge the gap with Asia's best."I want to improve my speed, grip and strength. Japanese and Korean players are very fast, so training there will help," he said.Born into a modest family, with his father working as a daily-wage labourer, Singh once trained without owning a judo uniform. Support from the govt's schemes and a privately funded athletes' training centre changed the course of his career."My life has changed because of this medal. More people have started noticing judo," he said. "But the best compliment came from my family. They told me, 'You have made the entire family proud.' That meant more than anything else."Having conquered injury to create CWG history, Singh's next aim is clear — turning a gritty comeback into an Asian Games podium finish.
Article Summary: Harsh Singh became India's first-ever men's judo gold medallist. The 23-year-old tore his ACL and meniscus while training at the Inspire Institute of Sport. Surgery followed in Oct last in Bengaluru before a year-long rehabilitation helped him return to competition.

Article Title: Aqib Nabi's India call-up will inspire Jammu & Kashmir cricketers: Bowling Coach Krishnakumar
Article Text:
Aquib Nabi has earned his maiden India call-up for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka (BCCI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

While there is ongoing debate over whether India’s Test selections increasingly favour IPL performances over sustained success in domestic cricket, Jammu & Kashmir bowling coach P Krishnakumar believes Aquib Nabi’s inclusion in the national squad will reinforce players’ faith in the traditional route to top-tier selection.Nabi, who was drafted into India’s squad for the upcoming Test series in Sri Lanka after Jasprit Bumrah’s injury, earned his place on the back of consistent Ranji Trophy performances. Reacting to the call-up, Krishnakumar said the selection sends an important message to aspiring cricketers.“I would not say it’s a late inclusion of Nabi in the national side because it is about picking the best combination for the country. It took some time but ultimately it happened. I’m sure this will definitely develop belief among aspiring cricketers across the country, especially in J&K, where players train in tough conditions. If they work hard and keep performing in the domestic circuit, they will eventually get their chance to play for the country,” Krishnakumar said.“In the IPL, because you are playing against the top players, it gives you a little bit of an edge.But Nabi’s selection will create belief. The selectors have reinforced the idea that if you perform consistently in domestic cricket, you will get an opportunity to play for the country,” he added.The coach said Nabi’s transformation into an international-ready fast bowler was the result of two years of meticulous preparation. “There is a lot of hard work behind this (selection). For the last two years, Nabi has upskilled his bowling,” he said. “We had several sessions where we worked on his swing, moving the ball, bowling on different pitches with different balls and in different conditions. We trained in the morning, afternoon and evening, in both very cold and very hot weather.The preparation was thorough. He has worked extremely hard to develop himself as a fast bowler.”According to Krishnakumar, succeeding on the flat wickets common in domestic cricket demanded a significant upgrade in Nabi’s skill set. “The pitches in domestic cricket are very flat and good for batting. To take wickets, you need high-quality skills. Aquib has worked very hard on that aspect,” he said. “Over the last two years, he was trying to get into the Indian team. I told him there was no point wasting time thinking over things he couldn’t control. What he could control was his preparation.”Assessing Nabi’s strengths, Krishnakumar described him as “fantastic when it comes to moving the ball” and said his natural length is well suited to red-ball cricket. At the same time, he urged patience, stressing that international cricket presents a far greater challenge than the domestic game. “Although he has done well on the India ‘A’ tour of Lanka, there is a difference in the quality of cricket,” Krishnakumar said. “We have to give him a chance and back him. Gautam bhai (head coach gautam Gambhir) will definitely give him the freedom and space to work. If he gets that backing, he will become a better bowler.”
Article Summary: Aquib Nabi has earned his maiden India call-up for the two-match Test series against Sri Lanka. Jammu & Kashmir bowling coach P Krishnakumar believes Nabi’s inclusion in the national squad will reinforce players’ faith in the traditional route to top-tier selection.

Article Title: Bodoland FC register emphatic 3-0 victory; Shillong Derby ends all square
Article Text:
Bodoland FC players after their win in Guwahati (Credit: Durand Cup Media)

KOLKATA: Fortunes took a turn for both Bodoland FC and FC1 after their second match of the 135th Durand Cup on Thursday.Having been subject to a painful loss in the opener against NorthEast United FC, Bodoland came back in dominating fashion with a 3-0 win over newcomers FC1 at Indira Gandhi Athletic Stadium in Guwahati.The visitors from the north to the Assam capital, however, could not follow up on their debut win against Karbi Anglong Morning Star FC despite staying ahead of Bodoland on the Group F table in second position with three points from two games. Bodoland, on third, also had three points from their two games.Robinson Rendon (57th min) put Bodoland ahead just past the hour, heading home from skipper Holicharan Narzary’s cross after twice missing similar chances earlier. Substitutes Rituraj Mohan (78’) and Aron Thapa (81’) then turned the lead into a rout inside four second-half minutes, both scoring within a quarter of an hour of being introduced, timing that owed at least as much to head coach Vikash Panthi’s reading of the game as it did to the finishers themselves.Earlier, at the coin toss, FC1 captain Ikhlaq Fayaz presented his Bodoland counterpart, Narzary, with a sapling, a symbol of the water-conservation and climate-awareness campaign that has quietly shaped FC1’s Durand Cup debut.Shillong derby ends in thrilling 2-2 draw: Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium in Shillong was witness to a classic state derby as Langsning FC made a brilliant comeback to hold Nongkseh SS&CC to a 2-2 draw in a Group E Shillong derby in the evening.After Shano Tariang (29’) and Hardycliff Nongbri had put Nongkseh ahead in the space of nine minutes, Mebanshngain Kurkalang (48’) and Syed Ahmed (50’) took just two minutes of the second half to restore parity to the game.Although both teams kept gunning for a late winner, the clubs had to share honours in the end. While Langsning kept their top spot in the group with four points from two matches, Nongkseh stayed on third, behind Shillong Lajong, with just a point from their two fixtures.Today’s Matches (August 7): SC Delhi vs Defenders FC (Group C), 4:00 PM, Birsa Munda Football Stadium, Ranchi; East Bengal FC vs South United FC (Group A), 7:00 PM, Vivekananda Yuba Bharati Krirangan, Kolkata
Article Summary: Bodoland FC beat FC1 3-0 in their second match of the 135th Durand Cup. Langsning FC held Nongkseh SS&CC to a thrilling 2-2 draw in a Group E Shillong derby in the evening.

Article Title: Lakshya Sen trains in Guwahati to prepare for BWF World Championships
Article Text:
Lakshya Sen (PTI Photos)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Lakshya Sen has made a strategic switch in his preparations for the BWF World Championships here, shifting his training from the Centre for Badminton Excellence (formerly PPBA) in Bengaluru to the BAI’s National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati’s Amingaon to acclimatise to challenging stadium conditions similar to the Indira Gandhi (IG) indoor stadium – the venue for the tournament beginning Aug 17.TOI has reliably learnt that India's leading men’s singles medal hope reached the 16-court, 40,000-square-foot facility on Thursday and began preparations with light sessions and warm-up matches. He is expected to train in Guwahati for a period of five days. Sen's primary foreign coach, South Korea's Yoo Yong-sung, has accompanied the shuttler to GuwahatiThe move is aimed at ensuring the same court drift and wind conditions that troubled him earlier this year do not derail his campaign at the Worlds. Sen wants to replicate the feel of a large indoor arena, where air-conditioning, high ceilings and swirling airflow significantly influence shuttle movement, unlike an academy setting.The decision stems from his experience at the India Open in Jan this year, where he heartbreakingly bowed out in the quarters after a 17-21, 21-13, 21-18 defeat to Chinese Taipei's Lin Chun-yi. Sen later admitted he struggled to adjust to the pronounced drift inside the stadium, particularly around the net, leading to crucial unforced errors before finding his rhythm too late.The Guwahati centre, designed with a high roof and spacious layout, offers conditions closer to those expected in Delhi, allowing Sen to fine-tune his control and anticipation under similar airflow patterns.It is learnt Sen is the only Indian player to move his training specifically for this purpose. While Ayush Shetty and PV Sindhu continue training in Bengaluru and Unnati Hooda remains at her base, India’s doubles and mixed doubles players are preparing at the Pullela Gopichand Academy in Hyderabad. Elite Bulgarian women’s doubles pair Gabriela and Stefani Stoeva are also training at the Guwahati facility ahead of the Worlds.
Article Summary: Lakshya Sen has made a strategic switch in his preparations for the BWF World Championships. Sen has shifted his training from the Centre for Badminton Excellence (formerly PPBA) in Bengaluru to the BAI’s National Centre of Excellence in Guwahati. The move is aimed at ensuring the same court drift and wind conditions that troubled him earlier this year do not derail his campaign at the Worlds.

Article Title: Indian hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton turns to AI to break language barrier
Article Text:
Indian team during a training session with Paddy Upton in Eindhoven on Thursday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: For foreign experts working with Indian athletes, language is often the biggest hurdle. With not every player comfortable communicating in English, overseas coaches and support staff frequently rely on translators within the team. The arrangement, while functional, can make conversations impersonal and, in sensitive situations, cause nuances to be lost in translation.To bridge that gap, Indian men’s hockey mental conditioning coach Paddy Upton has turned to artificial intelligence. Beginning with the upcoming FIH World Cup later this month, the renowned South African mental conditioning expert will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself.“It’s new to the sports world,” Upton told TOI in an exclusive interaction.“I would call it a digital twin or a digital version of me. Using artificial intelligence (AI), I have taken everything I’ve written and every conversation I’ve been able to record over 25 years of mental coaching, and trained an AI mental coaching twin of myself,” he explained.Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme with the help of some of India’s leading AI developers.Explaining the thinking behind the project, Upton, who has worked extensively with Indian athletes, including the men’s cricket team, said the idea stemmed from the limitations he faced while working with players who were not fluent in English.“With some players who don’t have good English skills, I wasn’t able to provide really good mental coaching support because of the language barrier. Previously, I would sit with a translator from within the team. But if it was something deeply personal, I knew it would either get lost in translation or the player would be hesitant because the translator was either a fellow player or a member of the support staff, which meant confidentiality was compromised. ”The players were introduced to the system on Wednesday.Explaining how it works, Upton said, “Now a player can have a conversation with me in Hindi. It’s like speaking on a WhatsApp call. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while I simultaneously see the English translation from wherever I am. The next day, I can sit with them and have a personal conversation as well.”While the languages are now restricted to Hindi and English, Upton added, “At this stage, it’s only in English and Hindi. This can fairly easily be expanded.”The 57-year-old stressed that the platform is designed to replicate his approach rather than function as a generic chatbot.“It’s an AI version of a personalised mental coach, but it is trained only on my information and speaks exactly as I would.”The timing, he said, was deliberate.“The idea was to have it ready for the World Cup so I could support players in a way that I haven't been able to before.”With a lot of his work with the team happening remotely, Upton believes the technology can significantly narrow the gap between him and the players.“It’s one of those things that's going to take time. The more they interact with it, the more they’ll understand it, and the richer the feedback and support it will be able to provide. It’s a very exciting development and a wonderful use of the technology now available to us,” he said.
Article Summary: Paddy Upton will introduce an AI-powered digital twin of himself at the World Cup. Upton spent the last four months developing the WhatsApp-based programme. The digital twin is trained to respond in Hindi, while Upton simultaneously sees the English translation from wherever he is.

Article Title: Former Indian cricketer Brijesh Patel calls for uniform coaching standards across cricket academies
Article Text:
Former cricketer Brijesh Patel (PTI Photo/Shailendra Bhojak)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BENGALURU: Former India batter Brijesh Patel on Thursday called for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies, saying the mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice.Speaking at the launch of the book, Developing Champions in Cricket by Vedam Jaishankar, the seasoned administrator said: “Over the last two decades, we have witnessed an explosion of cricket coaching centres. While this is wonderful for the growth of the game, it has also created a new challenge, a lack of standardisation. Every academy claims to have the best method, while every coach has a different philosophy. Every parent receives different advice and television experts have yet another opinion. The result is often confusing.”Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach, with every youngster requiring guidance tailored to their background and abilities. “Youngsters come from every background imaginable. Some come from cities with excellent facilities, while others travel from small towns.Their exposure, culture, skill levels and learning styles are different. A good coach first understands the child before teaching. And equally, a wise parent understands that every child's journey is unique,” he said.Patel also urged coaches and academies to focus on character-building. “Winning matches is important. Producing good human beings is even more important. Today, best practices are no longer optional,” Patel opined.Patel, who started an academy over four decades ago, underlined the need to create a safe and supportive environment for aspiring cricketers. “Parents want their children not just physically safe, but also emotionally secure. They must be protected from unhealthy influences, bullying, and unnecessary pressure. Creating that environment is the responsibility of every academy and every coach,” he added.
Article Summary: Brijesh Patel calls for greater standardisation across cricket coaching academies. Former India batter says mushrooming of centres has left young cricketers and parents dealing with conflicting advice. Patel stressed that coaching cannot follow a one-size-fits-all approach.

Article Title: Mohammedan SC removes Humayun Kabir as president after Rs 1.5 crore cheques bounce
Article Text:
Mohammedan SC removes Humayun Kabir as president

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

KOLKATA: In an extraordinary move, Mohammedan SC on Thursday removed Humayun Kabir as president of the club, just two months after the Aam Janata Unnayan Party (AJUP) founder was chosen to head the 135th-year-old institution’s administration.Ghazal Uz Zafar has been named the club’s new president with immediate effect.Soon after having been officially unveiled as the financially struggling club’s new president on June 6, Kabir promised to “solve the club’s financial problems.”However, it has been learnt that three of his cheques issued by him to the tune of Rs 1.5 crore to tackle the club’s financial requirements, eventually returned dishonoured by the bank as crisis over clearing players and staff members’ pending dues and other liabilities worsened.According to club sources, a notice was issued to Kabir seeking his explanation on unpaid funds but he didn’t respond to it.“The club called an executive committee meeting today and the decision to remove Mr Humayun Kabir was unanimous,” said a club official on Thursday.“The Executive Committee reviewed the Club’s prevailing financial position and discussed the immediate measures required to ensure financial and administrative continuity,” the club said in a statement.“The meeting also took note of the outstanding financial commitments of the Club and the urgent need to address its liabilities towards players, coaching staff, employees, statutory authorities, vendors and other creditors,” it further noted.
Article Summary: Mohammedan SC remove Humayun Kabir as president of the club. Ghazal Uz Zafar has been named the club’s new president with immediate effect. Kabir promised to “solve the club's financial problems” but three of his cheques issued by him to the tune of Rs 1.5 crore were returned dishonoured.

Article Title: ECB 'unhappy' as Ireland defy England's policy, host Afghanistan for ODI series
Article Text:
Afghanistan's Rashid Khan. (AP)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) is reportedly unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series, even though England continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments.The five-match ODI series between Ireland and Afghanistan began on Wednesday in Bready. According to a report in The Guardian, Ireland's decision to host Afghanistan could affect its future cricket ties with England.Ireland's move has put its relationship with the ECB under strain. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights.The ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid".However, England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events, where tournament points and titles are at stake.The ECB's policy is supported by the UK government, but Cricket Ireland has taken a different approach. Ireland has built close ties with the Afghanistan Cricket Board and is hosting five ODIs this month.Under a reciprocal arrangement, Ireland will tour the United Arab Emirates in March next year to play Afghanistan in one Test, three ODIs and three T20Is.England previously played one-off Tests against Ireland at Lord's before the home Ashes series in 2019 and 2023. Next year, however, England have chosen to play Bangladesh in a warm-up Test instead.England's men's team also faced Afghanistan in the Champions Trophy in Lahore last year.While the ECB does not schedule bilateral matches against Afghanistan, it has supported Afghan women cricketers in other ways. This summer, it organised a tour of England for the Afghan Refugee Women's team and invited them to attend the T20 World Cup final at Lord's.Most members of the Afghanistan women's team fled the country after the Taliban returned to power in 2021 and banned women's sport. Many of the players later settled in Australia.Afghanistan remain the only ICC Full Member without a women's cricket programme, but the ICC has not suspended them.Australia, South Africa and New Zealand have also refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan. Ireland, however, has joined the West Indies, Zimbabwe and the four Asian ICC Full Members in continuing bilateral cricket with Afghanistan.The ECB's relationship with Cricket Ireland has already been under pressure. England declined an invitation to take part in the proposed Euro Nations Cup next year, which would also feature Scotland, the Netherlands and Italy, citing a packed international schedule.England's men's team played a three-match T20I series in Ireland last September, but the ECB sent a second-string squad. No further men's matches between the two teams are currently scheduled.England's women's team, however, will host Ireland in a three-match ODI series next month.
Article Summary: England and Wales Cricket Board unhappy with Cricket Ireland for hosting Afghanistan in a five-match ODI series. England have refused to play bilateral cricket against Afghanistan because of the Taliban regime's restrictions on women's rights. ECB's stance is based on concerns over what its chair, Richard Thompson, has described as the Taliban's "gender apartheid" England continue to face Afghanistan in ICC events where tournament points and titles are at stake.

Article Title: WI vs PAK 2nd Test: Babar Azam's wait for Test century continues; Pakistan on brink of victory vs West Indies

's wait for Test hundred continues

NEW DELHI: Pakistan moved closer to a rare away Test win after reducing West Indies to 103/6 at stumps on Day 3 of the second and final Test. Despite West Indies holding a lead of 60 runs, the hosts have only four wickets left, giving Pakistan the upper hand heading into the fourth day.West Indies ended the day on 103/6, leading by 60 runs with only four wickets remaining.Pakistan will look to dismiss the remaining batters quickly on Day 4 and chase a modest target to secure their first away Test victory since 2023. West Indies, meanwhile, are aiming to complete a 2-0 series sweep after winning the opening Test by 90 runs.Pakistan began the day still behind West Indies' first-innings total of 344, but Abdullah Shafique produced a superb unbeaten 160 to guide his team to 387.His innings helped Pakistan secure a 43-run first-innings lead before the visitors were bowled out.Left-arm spinner Jomel Warrican starred for West Indies with six wickets for 112 runs. He cleaned up the Pakistan lower order after already removing key batters earlier in the innings.Pakistan captain Babar Azam once again missed out on a Test century.He was run out for 88 after a brilliant direct hit from Brandon King ended his 183-run partnership with Shafique.Pakistan were still trailing by 63 runs when the wicket fell.Babar attempted a quick single after pushing the ball into the off side, but Shafique changed his mind and sent him back. King collected the ball and hit the stumps with a flat throw, leaving Babar short of his ground despite a desperate dive.It was Babar's highest Test score in 35 innings, but he is still waiting for his first Test century since scoring one against New Zealand in Karachi in December 2022.Brandon King's brilliant fielding effort came at a cost.The West Indies batter injured his lower back after landing awkwardly while throwing down the stumps. Warrican then bowled Mohammad Rizwan for 18 with the second new ball and later finished the innings by taking three wickets in four deliveries to complete a six-wicket haul.West Indies made a solid start to their second innings as Tagenarine Chanderpaul and Kavem Hodge added 40 runs for the opening wicket.However, Pakistan's spinners quickly took control.Sajid Khan removed Chanderpaul and Amir Jangoo before West Indies recovered through a partnership between Shai Hope and captain Roston Chase.The visitors then lost three wickets in the final five overs of the day. Sajid trapped Hope lbw for 15 and dismissed Jayden Seales for a two-ball duck. On the last ball of the day, Chase lost his concentration and chipped a simple return catch to Ali Usman after scoring 17.Sajid finished the day with figures of 4/32, while Usman picked up 2/29.

Article Title: Once masters of the turn, now haunted by it: India's spin paradox ahead of Sri Lanka Tests
Article Text:
(IANS) Premier Indian left-arm wrist-spinner Kuldeep Yadav

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Fighting anxiety

Head coach Gautam Gambhir, expectedly, was his fiery self when he delivered a short speech in Colombo as the Indian team began its preparation for the two-Test series against Sri Lanka. The numbers of the two teams over the last decade suggest India should get their bid to qualify for next year's World Test Championship (WTC) final off to a good start over the next three weeks. Yet, there's unmistakable unease edginess in the camp.The unease essentially stems from the remarkable depreciation in the performances in spin-friendly conditions. That Indian team has carried a host of spinners as net bowlers again indicates that the team management is expecting outright spinning conditions in the two Tests.The abject surrender at home against New Zealand and South Africa in Gambhir's tenure has ensured this series has generated more interest than it did in the last decade when India enjoyed overwhelming dominance over Sri Lanka. This is a banana peel series and India could trip on the spin threat.It's ironic to think to that India's Test cricket fed off spin and the team became a powerhouse when spin became a major force in a Test match.India's batting against spin served as tutorials for the rest of the world. Spinners, across generations, largely carried the burden of turning fortunes. It all now seems to be disappearing like poof of dust.India's batting has largely been crumbling against trying spin bowling—both at home and overseas for more than half a decade. The raging turners at home saw Cheteshwar Pujara and Ajinkya Rahane's careers come to a screeching end before it eventually accounted for Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma. It was Ravichandran Ashwin and Ravindra Jadeja 's class that shored up India against the touring teams. If one closely analyses India's defeats at home, it will be difficult to go past the fact that Indian spinners have been consistently out-bowled.Former India left-arm spinner Murali Kartik feels this series will truly signal the passing of the spin baton for Indian cricket. Kuldeep Yadav, the forever man waiting in the wings, will be in the face of the action. "It will be an important series for Kuldeep. Everyone expected that the baton would pass smoothly once Ashwin left. It hasn't quite happened yet. Jadeja is in the fag end of his career. So, it will be exciting to see how Kuldeep and Manav Suthar, who has been seen as the one to carry India's spin bowling forward, go about it," Kartik told TOI.Interestingly, when India played on pitches that weren't exactly square turners last home season, the Indian spinners lacked the incisiveness that made them a feared breed in international cricket."For me, it's important that Kuldeep is fresh. Because a lot of his bowling depends on his action because a lot goes into it. If he is fresh then, he will have the momentum going towards the batter," Kartik opined while adding that Suthar will hold the key. "Suthar is like a breath of fresh air. Even against Afghanistan, he looked so good even with Kuldeep and Washington bowling from the other end," he said.The most important thing that the Indian spinners need to be careful about is not getting carried seeing turning pitches. "What Mitch Santner and Simon Harmer did well in India was they bowled at the right pace and never left their lengths. Even if they went for an odd boundary. Indian spinners couldn't do it in those two series at home. They have to give the batter a false sense of confidence," Kartik warnedKartik also warned against anxiety in such conditions. For Suthar, it will be important to gain control over the Kookaburra ball. "Suthar has to ensure that he doesn't get anxious. The good thing is that he recently bowled with the Kookaburra ball which has a flatter seam in Sri Lanka for India 'A'. He will need to rein himself in at times," he said.For Kuldeep, the team management under Gambhir has shown little faith in him for his batting capabilities which gave Washington Sundar the edge over him. "It will be completely up to him to find a way to balance it between his batting and bowling. He is a capable Test batter. He had shown it against England at home," Kartik claimed.It will be a more challenging tour mentally than one presumed. A slip up here and Indian cricket will need a lot of work to get up on its feet again.
Article Summary: Former India spinner Murali Kartik feels this series will truly signal the passing of the spin baton for Indian cricket. India's batting has largely been crumbling against trying spin bowling for more than half a decade. The raging turners at home saw Cheteshwar Pujara's careers come to a screeching end.

Article Title: Vinay Kumar set to return home as Karnataka head coach

BENGALURU: In one of the most high-profile appointments of coaches in Karnataka cricket, the KSCA has roped in former Indian pacer and state skipper R Vinay Kumar as the head coach for the upcoming season.The 42-year-old, the most successful captain of Karnataka, is learnt to have been cleared by the Cricket Administrative Committee (CAC), which includes Anil Kumble, Rahul Dravid, Sunil Joshi, Javagal Srinath and Venkatesh Prasad. Vinay’s appointment, along with that of the other men's and women’s coaching staff, will be ratified at the managing committee meeting likely to be held on August 13.Vinay, apart from being a talent scout for Mumbai Indians, has also been the bowling coach of MI Emirates in the ILT20. A seasoned commentator, Vinay is also likely to become the highest-paid coach ever roped in by the KSCA.The state team, which finished runners-up in the 2025-26 Ranji Trophy , is in a transitional phase with many youngsters being bloodied in and Devdutt Padikkal handed over the reins of the team.Vinay made his Ranji Trophy debut against Bengal under the captaincy of J Arun Kumar. He launched his career with the wicket of opposition skipper Rohan Gavaskar.He moved out of Karnataka in 2019 and spent a year with the Pondicherry team. After going without an IPL contract or state team the following season, he called time on his career in 2021.Vinay was among the key members of the golden period of Karnataka cricket between 2013-15. During this phase, with Vinay leading the team and J Arun Kumar as the head coach, Karnataka won two trophies each in the Ranji Trophy, Vijay Hazare Trophy and Irani Trophy.Vinay brings with him the experience of having earned an India cap in all three formats, seven major domestic titles as captain and 504 first-class wickets from 139 matches at an average of 22.44, of which a record 442 are Ranji Trophy scalps.Vinay, who coached Hubli Tigers in the recently concluded Maharaja Trophy KSCA T20 tournament, held a meeting with fast bowlers on Monday, with the likes of Vyshak Vijaykumar and Vidwath Kaverappa, along with junior bowlers, in attendance. He will hold a session for spinners on Friday. With the ratification of his appointment coming through next week, the former pacer is expected to hold a two-week camp at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium later this month before the Dr (Capt) K Thimmappiah Memorial Cricket Tournament, which is the precursor to the red-ball season.Vinay takes over from Yere Goud, who has moved on to the BCCI Centre of Excellence in the role of a batting coach.
Article Summary: Former Indian pacer and state skipper R Vinay Kumar is the head coach for the upcoming season. The 42-year-old is learnt to have been cleared by the Cricket Administrative Committee (CAC), which includes Anil Kumble, Rahul Dravid, Sunil Joshi, Javagal Srinath and Venkatesh Prasad.

Article Title: England fast bowler John Turner retires from cricket at 25

England fast bowler John Turner has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 25 after struggling with injuries.The Hampshire pacer, who represented England in four international matches in 2024, still had two years left on his county contract. He also held an ECB development contract until late last year.Turner, who was born in Johannesburg, played two ODIs and two T20Is during England's tour of the West Indies in late 2024, taking three wickets. He had also built a strong record across domestic cricket.However, he has not played since June last year after suffering a back stress fracture. Turner said his injury history played a major role in his decision to step away from the game.An economics and finance graduate from the University of Exeter, Turner said he now wants to move on to the next stage of his life."It was always my dream to play professional and international cricket, and doing so for Hampshire and England has been nothing short of living out those same childhood dreams," Turner said in a statement."I have, however, decided to retire from the game, and as you can imagine, this has been one of the hardest decisions I've had to make.The stress fracture, which has sidelined me for over a year, as well as my injury record, naturally made me think of my future both as a cricketer and away from the game, and subsequently, I decided now was the right time to pursue my next challenge."The five years I have been able to call myself a professional cricketer for Hampshire have been the greatest five years possible. From the day I joined the club in pursuit of a dream, everyone was extremely welcoming, and this never changed."The opportunity and belief the club showed in me are something I could never thank them enough for. I have experienced more over the last few years than I could ever imagine, and none of that would be possible without the support from everyone at the club."Turner studied at Hilton College in South Africa before moving to the United Kingdom for university through his British passport, which he holds through his English mother.He joined Hampshire in 2021 after a successful trial and earned his first England call-up in 2023 after impressing in The Hundred.
Article Summary: England fast bowler John Turner has announced his retirement from professional cricket at the age of 25. The Hampshire pacer represented England in four international matches in 2024. Turner has not played since June last year after suffering a back stress fracture. He still had two years left on his county contract.

Article Title: 'Huge ask': ECB explains why Harry Brook missed out as Joe Root returns as Test captain
Article Text:
Harry Brook (ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

England's decision to bring Joe Root back as Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement may have surprised many, but the England and Wales Cricket Board believes it is the right move for both the present and the future.With Harry Brook already serving as England's white-ball captain and acting as Stokes' deputy in the Test side, the 27-year-old had been widely tipped to inherit the red-ball leadership. Instead, the selectors opted to hand the reins back to Root, who previously captained England before Stokes took over.ECB selector Marcus North explained that while Brook is already proving himself as a leader in white-ball cricket, the board does not want to overload him by asking him to captain across all three formats.“I think Harry Brook is obviously a fantastic player for us in all formats. Incredibly important. I think his leadership in the white-ball game is maturing with every series. I think we’ve seen that through our T20 side, getting to No. 1 in the world during the summer, albeit I think we’ve slipped back to No. 2, but we’re certainly one of the best teams in the world in T20 cricket. And we have won our last two ODI series building into the World Cup," North told Sky Sports.Brook has overseen England's rise in white-ball cricket, with the team reaching the top of the T20I rankings during the summer before slipping to second. England have also won their last two ODI series as preparations continue for next year's ODI World Cup.North said the ECB remains fully committed to Brook as a future Test captain but believes the timing is not right given his existing responsibilities in white-ball cricket.According to the selector, managing England in all three international formats would be a significant challenge for any player, making Root's experience a valuable asset for the Test side at this stage.“So, you know, he’s doing a fantastic job there with an eye on the World Cup at the back end of next year, working with Brendon (McCullum). That’s a key focus, and leading in all three formats is a huge ask for any captain."“I’ve no doubt that the time will come for Harry, but we’re very blessed that we’ve got someone like Joe (Root), who’s so experienced and is going to do such a great job this time round, with Harry and Brendon working in the white-ball space," he added.The appointment marks Root's second stint as England's Test captain, with the ECB choosing experience over succession planning as they begin a new chapter following Stokes' retirement.
Article Summary: Joe Root has been appointed as England's Test captain after Ben Stokes' retirement. Harry Brook had been tipped to inherit the red-ball leadership. The ECB does not want to overload Brook by asking him to captain in all three formats. Root's experience will be a valuable asset for the Test side at this stage.

Article Title: Ajinkya Rahane snubs MS Dhoni, Virat Kohli; names India's greatest-ever cricketer

Former India captain Ajinkya Rahane has picked Sachin Tendulkar as the greatest Indian cricketer of all time, shortly after bringing the curtain down on his playing career. Rahane , who recently announced his retirement from all forms of cricket during an episode of Stick to Cricket, was asked to name India's greatest-ever cricketer. While acknowledging that the choice was far from straightforward, the former batter eventually settled on Tendulkar.“I think it’s very hard to take one name but… probably Sachin Tendulkar. I think all the eras," Rahane said.Tendulkar enjoyed a remarkable international career that stretched across 24 years, representing India from November 15, 1989, to November 16, 2013. During that period, he featured in 664 international matches, including 200 Tests, 463 ODIs and one T20I.The batting icon scored 15,921 runs in Tests, 18,426 in ODIs and 10 in T20Is, finishing as the highest run-scorer in the history of both Test and ODI cricket. He also remains the only player to have appeared in 200 Test matches and holds the record for the most ODI appearances.Tendulkar was a central figure in India's triumphant 2011 ICC Men's ODI World Cup campaign, adding the coveted trophy to an already glittering career.As captain, he led India in 25 Tests, registering four wins, nine defeats and 12 draws. In ODIs, Tendulkar captained the side in 73 matches, winning 23, losing 43, with one tie and six no-results.Rahane made his international debut in a T20I against England at Manchester on August 31, 2011, and went on to represent India across all three formats between 2011 and 2023.The Mumbai batter had the opportunity to share the dressing room with Tendulkar on mult ipl e occasions. He played one Test alongside the legendary batter for India and had earlier been his teammate at Mumbai Indians during the 2009 IPL season, apart from representing Mumbai together in domestic cricket.Across a career spanning more than 12 years, Rahane played most of his international cricket under MS Dhoni and Virat Kohli . He was a key member of India's historic 2018-19 Test series-winning squad in Australia before captaining the team to another memorable series victory there in 2020-21.Rahane also joined an exclusive list of Indian cricketers to captain the national side in all three formats. He finished his career with Test centuries in Australia, England and New Zealand, while representing six IPL franchises: Mumbai Indians, Rajasthan Royals , Rising Pune Supergiants, Delhi Capitals, Kolkata Knight Riders and Chennai Super Kings .

During the ceremony, the Commonwealth Games flag was officially handed over to India as Ahmedabad prepares to host the next edition in 2030.According to an official release, "deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi formally presented the Commonwealth Games Flag, with full honour and dignity, to chief minister Bhupendra Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar."Para-athletes Rakesh Bhatt and Rohit Majgul, who represented Gujarat at the Glasgow Commonwealth Games, were present during the ceremony. Para table tennis player Sonal Patel also attended.The release added, "The Commonwealth Games Flag will now remain in Gujarat until the 2030 Commonwealth Games. Along with advancing Prime Minister Narendra Modi's 'Fit India' vision, it will serve as an inspiration for athletes and symbolise the commencement of preparations for the upcoming event."Speaking to reporters after arriving at Ahmedabad Airport earlier in the day, Sanghavi said the city aims to set a new standard for hosting the Commonwealth Games."These Games will be organised with grandeur and with the best possible arrangements for the athletes. They will be conducted in such a way that every athlete can deliver his best performance," the deputy CM said.Sanghavi, who also holds the sports portfolio, said the Gujarat government remains committed to taking forward Prime Minister Narendra Modi's Fit India movement and anti-drug campaign."We will advance the anti-drug campaign and the Fit India Movement so that the youth of the country receive maximum opportunities in the sports sector. The Gujarat Government is working towards this goal. Under the guidance of the Government of India, we will continue to move this work forward," he said.
Article Summary: The Commonwealth Games flag was formally presented to Gujarat chief minister Bhupendra Patel on Wednesday. Deputy chief minister Harsh Sanghavi handed over the flag to Patel during the state cabinet meeting in Gandhinagar. Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra and Indian Olympic Association (IOA) president PT Usha attended the ceremony.

Article Title: Reality check after Commonwealth Games 2026: India’s boxing renaissance to face ultimate Asian exam
Article Text:
New Delhi, Aug 04 (ANI): Union Minister Kiren Rijiju in a group photograph with Indian boxing contingent (@KirenRijiju X/ANI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India’s record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism, but the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. After returning from Glasgow with a historic haul of seven gold and three silver medals, India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.The CWG triumph underlined the country’s growing depth, particularly in women’s boxing. Sakshi Chaudhary (51kg), Preeti Pawar (54kg), Jaismine Lamboria (57kg), Priya Ghanghas (60kg) and Arundhati Choudhary (70kg) struck gold, while Sachin Siwach (60kg) and Ankush Panghal (80kg) topped the podium in the men’s competition. Olympic medallist Lovlina Borgohain, Jadumani Singh and Narender Berwal added silver medals.The challenge in Aichi-Nagoya, however, will be on an entirely different scale. Unlike the Commonwealth Games, the Asian Games will feature continental powerhouses such as Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, China, Chinese Taipei, Japan and North Korea — nations that have consistently dominated the World Championships and the Olympics.Uzbek stars Mirazizbek Mirzakhalilov and Bobo-Usmon Baturov, along with Kazakhstan’s Kairat Yeraliyev and Ablaikhan Zhussupov, are expected to headline a field packed with world-class talent.India will also be without two of its Commonwealth champions. Jaismine (57kg) and Arundhati (70kg) will miss out because their weight categories do not feature in the Asian Games programme, depriving the country of two genuine medal prospects.“The Asian Games for us is like the Olympics,” Boxing Federation of India president Ajay Singh said. “The best teams in the world today are Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and India, and all three are in Asia. Add a strong Chinese contingent and you understand why it is much tougher. You can’t replicate this (CWG) performance at the Asian Games. But if you win a sizeable number of medals at the Asian Games, you can be hopeful of winning medals at the Olympics too.Women’s head coach Santiago Nieva shared a similar assessment while insisting the team remains on the right path.“We can’t guarantee that we will win gold all the time, but we are on the right track. We know how strong the field will be at the Asian Games. The boxers are aware that they can’t sit on their success,” he said.India had returned with one silver and three bronze medals from the 2022 Asian Games in Hangzhou. The Glasgow CWG showcased the strides the boxing contingent has made. But it’ll be Aichi-Nagoya that is going to reveal whether the progress is enough to challenge Asia’s finest and signal genuine medal potential for the 2028 Olympics.
Article Summary: India's record-breaking boxing campaign at the Commonwealth Games has generated plenty of optimism. But the celebrations will quickly give way to a far sterner test when attention shifts to the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, from Sept 19 to Oct 4. India’s boxers now head into what many within the sport regard as the closest thing to the Olympics.

Article Title: Pakistan boxer Qudratullah ‘goes missing’ in Glasgow after Commonwealth Games campaign

Pakistani boxer Qudratullah has reportedly gone missing in Glasgow, just hours before the country’s Commonwealth Games contingent was scheduled to leave for home.According to a report by Pakistani outlet Geo News, sources in the Pakistan Boxing Federation said Qudratullah was last seen in his hotel room at around 2am. Officials later checked his room and found that he was no longer there.The Pakistan team was due to gather in the hotel lobby at 9am before leaving for Pakistan. However, Qudratullah could not be found when officials checked his room, sources said.His passport and return ticket are reportedly still with the team manager. The incident is not the first such case involving a Pakistani boxer abroad, with another promising boxer, Zohaib, reportedly going missing during an international tour of Italy last year.Pakistan’s 21-member contingent finished the 2026 Commonwealth Games with only one medal. Boxer Fatima Zahra won bronze in the women’s 60kg category, giving Pakistan its only podium finish at the Games.The result was Pakistan’s lowest medal tally since the 1998 Commonwealth Games, when the country won one silver. Pakistan had also returned without a medal from the 1990 edition, making Glasgow its poorest CWG campaign in 36 years.Fatima made history by becoming the first Pakistani female boxer to win a Commonwealth Games medal and was later chosen to carry the national flag at the closing ceremony.Pakistan’s biggest medal hope, Olympic javelin champion Arshad Nadeem, also failed to finish on the podium after serving as the country’s flagbearer at the opening ceremony.

Article Title: ‘Like preparing for IIT and UPSC together’: Father Murali shares Sreeshankar’s comeback story
Article Text:
Murali Sreeshankar

KOCHI: S Murali gave an unusual analogy to describe the struggles his son, long jumper Sreeshankar Murali, undertook to regain full fitness after a career-threatening knee injury he sustained two years ago.“Sreeshankar’s comeback was as difficult as preparing for the IIT and Civil Services simultaneously,” he told TOI.Murali is currently near Prague, where he is closely monitoring his son’s training ahead of a busy stretch that begins with the World Athletics Continental Tour (silver level) meet in Bhubaneswar on Aug 22, followed by next month’s Asian Games in Japan.“Sreeshankar’s training now revolves around strength and conditioning, along with the prehab and rehab programme designed by coach Wayne Lombard. There is very little time to work on technique. The priority is to protect the knee on his take-off leg,” Murali said.His IIT-UPSC analogy aptly captures the magnitude of the challenge Sreeshankar faced after suffering the devastating injury just months before the 2024 Paris Olympics.Two years later, the journey came full circle when the 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week’s Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.“Of all the medals Sreeshankar has won, this one gives me the greatest satisfaction because of the circumstances under which he achieved it. It reflects his mental toughness and hunger,” Murali said.The conditions in Glasgow were anything but favourable.“It was around 12 degrees Celsius with drizzle and strong winds, making the runway tricky,” Murali said. Despite the difficult conditions, Sreeshankar produced a best jump of 8.09m to finish second.The performance inevitably brought back painful memories of 2024, when the family received a grim diagnosis after Sreeshankar tore the patellar tendon in his take-off leg.“The doctors in Mumbai had not seen an injury like this. I thought he would never be able to walk again,” Murali recalled.“They told us it wasn’t a common sports injury but the kind usually seen after a serious car accident. His knee was completely ruptured.”Determined to find the best treatment, Murali travelled nearly 1,900 miles with his son to Doha’s Aspetar Hospital. “The surgeons reconstructed his knee using four screws.”The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process.The painstaking recovery paid rich dividends. Since returning to elite competition, Sreeshankar has consistently cleared the eight-metre mark, including a season’s best of 8.38m at the Inter-State Championships in Bhubaneswar in June.“There is no time to bask in the Commonwealth Games glory,” Murali said, pointing to the demanding schedule ahead.Sreeshankar will now turn his attention to the Asian Games in Japan, where he hopes to upgrade the silver medal he won at the previous edition in Hangzhou.“With everything Sreeshankar has gone through, he has every reason to believe he can stand on top of the podium at the Asian Games,” Murali concluded.
Article Summary: Sreeshankar Murali suffered a career-threatening knee injury two years ago. The Palakkad athlete spent more than eight months away from competition before beginning the long rehabilitation process. The 27-year-old clinched the silver medal at last week's Commonwealth Games.

Article Title: 'You are still a role model': CWG medallist Tejaswin Shankar hails Vinesh Phogat, recalls 2018 memories

Commonwealth Games 2026 bronze medallist Tejaswin Shankar has expressed his gratitude to star wrestler Vinesh Phogat for her words of encouragement after a knee injury forced him to withdraw from the high jump event at the recent Commonwealth Games.Shankar, a two-time Commonwealth Games medallist, was forced out of the high jump after his long-standing knee problem flared up during his opening attempt. Rooting for you as always."Remembering Vinesh’s support, Shankar thanked her publicly and recalled how she had helped him feel comfortable during his first Commonwealth Games in 2018.Remembering her support, Shankar replied, “Thank you, Vinesh ji for your motivating words.
